title: Produce and round canonical Clifford coefficients on a reversible local tape
body:
This connects the five canonical weights from #7821 to the physical divider in #7820. The reversible tape accepts a factored four-qubit Clifford lift, a queried Pauli label, and a list of Gaussian-unit-weighted repeated matrix units. It determines support and absolute phase from the runtime labels, adds the real and imaginary numerators, and rounds their signed sum to the requested binary precision with nearest-even ties. The output is copied and all scratch and routing tracks are uncomputed.

All five Hadamard ranks use the same exact component denominator **4,116,898,131,384,729,600**. A single rank-four coefficient forces it. The attainable complex numerator lattice and the minimum number of nonzero records are also determined at each rank. A separate classical compiler builds the factored binary action and, when supplied, preserves the absolute Gaussian matrix gauge. Its setup cost is outside the per-query tape invoice.

For the public three-record, nonidentity input at 48 fraction bits the output is **$(0,-1701)/2^{48}$**. The actual local program uses 458 ten-track sites, 97,574 NOTs, 849,046 CNOTs, 171,478 Toffolis and 1,353,992 head moves including the return home. Rounding the three contributions first gives a different answer. The verifier checks the complete local execution against the unrounded exact coefficient. An independent Bruhat check compares 12,800 phased matrix entries on 50 explicit four-qubit gate words and tests all 720 embedded two-qubit symplectic maps.

The pinned costs and kernels build on the published work in #7772, #7816, #7820 and #7821. The result prices one specified readout interface and preserves the selected multiplication exponent.

All 8 registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and in a read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The source-history, committed-byte, mode and export-inventory checks passed.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-reversible-coefficient-readout
```
